comments.body:
Six-change stack LANDED on origin/main, plus F9.

Merged in original order: d6a1446eea03 Partition ticket types (F3), 5a6f76b126b6 MCP model registry (F5), 3448f22493d1 reducer status vocabulary (F6), eed080bfaf05 cycle-capable relations (F4), 03648d47d4c8 create ticket-type vocabulary (F7), 9cae469af953 op-cert kind vocabulary (F2). Change 2547 (F9, source-kind vocabulary from LAYER_ORDER) merged as a3e4939062d6.

I verified the gates myself before submitting rather than taking the subagent report at face value: all six at LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, submittable true, 0 unresolved. Submitted the top of the stack, which submitted its ancestors; all six now MERGED and present on origin/main.

Root cause of the long Verified -1, confirmed independently by two paths. NEITHER hypothesis in the original brief was right, and no CI run in this stack ever contained a single FAILED tests/ line.
(a) src/rebar/types.py is a GENERATED file ("DO NOT EDIT BY HAND", produced by python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types). F3 hand-added PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES/PLAN_REVIEW_REVIEWED_TYPES and F7 hand-added TICKET_TYPES; CI regenerates and diffs, the hand-added block vanishes, every commit in the stack fails the public-types drift gate. Fixed by adding a declaration seam to the generator (_DERIVED_VOCABULARIES keyed by the common.schema.json def each block derives from), so the constants stay in rebar.types as a stdlib-only leaf AND survive regeneration.
(b) The earlier failures were environmental: the Gerrit checkout step got HTTP 504 for 60s during a sustained availability fault that also hit unrelated changes 2541/2542/2545. No fix warranted; new patchsets re-triggered CI.

Two caveats recorded rather than buried. The subagent hit a near-miss during the rebase — a git commit --amend while stopped on a CONFLICT rather than an edit stop folded 2536 into 2535 and collapsed the stack to five; it aborted and redid the rebase correctly, and the final six commits kept their original Change-Ids with no duplicate changes. And it killed a full tests/unit run still going after 23 minutes on this contended box, so no full local suite was personally observed green — CI Verified +1 on every patchset is the authoritative run covering that.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Closes: 8 of 15 children now closed. Closed this round after verifying ACs against the merged tree (59 tests green on gerrit/main, plus the cli-reference, MCP-model-drift and types-drift gates all clean there): 91b0 F8, bc66, 0af1 F14, 70f5 F9, a516 F6, 6850 F2, 62eb F5, cacb F4. bc66 closing reported unblocked: 1daf, so F11 is genuinely unblocked by the edge.

TWO CLOSES REFUSED, correctly, and I did not force them.

ce8f (F7) and e755 (F3) were refused because their merged commits touch src/rebar/schemas/gen_types.py — and for ce8f also src/rebar/types.py — which their recorded file_impact never declared. The gate is right: that work DID go beyond the reviewed plan. It was added later, by the subagent fixing the public-types drift gate, once we learned types.py is GENERATED and hand-added constants vanish on regeneration. The reviewed plans predate that discovery and describe only the consuming modules.

The gate names two paths: declare the files (a MATERIAL plan change that invalidates the attestation and requires a fresh review-plan), or --force. Agents must not use force overrides, and this is exactly the case the prohibition is for — forcing would close a ticket whose recorded plan does not describe what actually shipped, leaving no durable record that the generator seam was part of this work.

So I widened file_impact on both to declare gen_types.py (and types.py for ce8f) with reasons naming why the generator must emit the constant, and re-ran review-plan on both. They close once those return PASS+signed.

Verdict: stale-material — the epic plan-review attestation pinned 14 children and the epic now has 16. That is accurate: two children were added DURING execution, both for good reasons and both recorded at the time.
- eagleeyed-commutable-mantisray (bc66), the _cli/_registry.py validation split, filed when F11 turned out to need Route headroom that a file sitting at exactly 800 lines could not give it.
- florid-cookable-fly (90cb), filed when the plan-review gate caught a seventh consumer of the plan-review-exempt vocabulary that the F3 plan had missed.

So the epic genuinely is not the epic that was reviewed, and the gate is right to say so. The named remedy is to re-run review-plan on the epic and retry the close; that is running now. No force override was used, and none will be.

One detail from the refusal worth keeping, because it settles a question I raised earlier in this session: the gate states explicitly that ticking an AC checkbox is attestation-SAFE — box state is normalized out of the material fingerprint, so a tick is never the cause of staleness. My earlier observation that ticking left the verdict unchanged was right, and now it is confirmed by the implementation rather than by inference.

Every one of the 16 children is closed and all 14 epic changes are MERGED. The epic close is the only step left.

Epic AC verification, done before ticking.

AC1 — every child closed, each either deriving the mirrored value from its canonical source or adding a gate that fails on divergence. All 16 children are closed and each close passed the completion verifier, which is what AC1 names as the verification. Categorised: derivations are F1 (KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES), F2 (op-cert kinds), F3 (plan-review type partition), F4 (blocking relations), F6 (reducer statuses), F7 (composer types), F9 (source kinds), F11 (cross-session warn set) and florid-cookable-fly (bare-exempt set); divergence gates are F5 (MCP model drift), F8 (three-way relation parity), F10 (docs enumeration census), F12 (exit-codes conformance), F13 (gate step ids) and F14 (mutating-verb prose census).

ONE HONEST EXCEPTION, recorded rather than glossed: eagleeyed-commutable-mantisray (bc66) satisfies neither clause literally. It is the _cli/_registry.py validation split — a structural PREREQUISITE added mid-epic because _registry.py sat at exactly 800 lines and F11 could not add its Route flag without exceeding the cap. It remediates no mirror of its own. AC1 was written for the 14 inventory mirrors; bc66 and florid-cookable-fly were added during execution. florid-cookable-fly does derive, so it satisfies AC1 on its own terms; bc66 is an enabler and I am ticking AC1 with that exception stated rather than pretending it fits.

AC2 — no fix collapses a DISTINCT CONCEPT. Verified mechanically rather than by assertion: I took the union of files touched by all 14 merged epic commits (37 files) and intersected it with the files behind the inventory's nine rejected families. The intersection is EMPTY. In particular scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py was never touched, so F14 did not walk into the MUTATION_VERBS name-collision the inventory explicitly warns about — F14 touched only scripts/gen_cli_reference.py and the two prose copies.

Two places where the epic actively declined to collapse a distinct concept, which is AC2 working rather than merely not failing:
- F3: the gate found a seventh consumer at workflow_ops.py:108. I did NOT fold it in, because that set is the exempt set MINUS bug — a bug takes a light advisory review tier rather than a bare exempt PASS, so merging them would have silently deleted that tier. Split out as florid-cookable-fly and fixed separately with its own derivation.
- F11: WHICH verbs warn cross-session is a policy judgement; the ticket changed only that the spellings must BE route names, and pinned membership against the exact 14 to prove no policy moved.

Method note: my first attempt at the AC2 census returned zero files, which I nearly reported as 'no intersection'. It was an empty result from a broken git invocation, not evidence. Re-ran it correctly, and then found my SHA list covered only 11 of the 14 commits and completed it — the missing three included F11, whose _execute.py edit had been absent from the census.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

Sibling epic `wide-wimpy-insect` (87cb-7121-a3b6-4606, Track I — reduce defect introduction)
commissioned a sweep for hand-maintained representation mirrors: one canonical fact with two
masters that can drift apart. Representation drift is the dominant sub-mechanism of the
product-logic defect category in the R2S1 mechanism read.

The sweep is complete and its inventory is committed at `reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md`
(task `yogic-soapstone-takin`, f9b9-83ad-931c-4833). It examined **77 candidate sets** across five
areas and found **14 genuine mirrors, 5 already drifted**. That task's deliverable was the
inventory; the remediation is this epic.

## Scope

One child per genuine mirror, each proposing a named fix pattern — generate-from-canonical,
add-parity-check, add-census-assertion-to-existing-test, or add-route-flag. Each child carries its
own two-master `file:line` evidence and a severity, and links `discovered_from` the sweep task.

Recommended order (highest value first):

1. **F1** — reducer event-type dispatch has two masters. Not yet drifted, but a known type with no
   handler is folded into a snapshot and its file retired: silent permanent data loss.
2. **F12** — `docs/exit-codes.md` is drifted from `ROUTES` today, in both directions, while
   claiming to be pinned by a test whose entire assertion is one string check.
3. **F13** — `_validate_gate_step_ids` already exists and is called for plan-review only; the same
   silent-degradation class is left open for code-review and completion-verification. NOT one line
   each: the validator's signature is `(doc, required, *, gate_name)`, and the only `required` set
   that exists is `_PLAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED_STEP_IDS`. So each remaining gate needs (a) its OWN
   required-step-id frozenset, naming the step ids that gate's dispatcher logic actually
   references — code-review reuses `STEP_VERIFY`/`STEP_DECIDE` plus its finalization cluster, and
   completion-verification has its own — and (b) a call sited right after that gate's
   `_gate_doc(...)` load, mirroring the plan-review call. The child must DERIVE each set from the
   dispatcher's real references rather than copying plan-review's, or the check passes
   vacuously while still permitting the rename it exists to catch.

Then the remaining HIGH findings (F5, F3), the MEDIUM ones (F4, F10, F2, F6, F7), and the LOW ones
(F8, F9, F11, F14).

## Method note carried forward

The sweep's most reliable discriminator, worth applying to any future audit: **a comment claiming
"single-sourced" or "kept in lockstep" is a marker for an UNENFORCED mirror.** All four such claims
in the tree were false. Equally: equal counts hide drift — F12's two sides both had 78 rows and
different members, so only a set difference found it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: every child is closed, each having either generated the mirrored value from its canonical
      source or added a gate that fails on divergence. Verified by each child's own close.
- [x] AC2: no fix collapses a DISTINCT CONCEPT. The inventory's rejected list records nine candidate
      families that look duplicated but are semantically different predicates; a remediation that
      merges one of those introduces a defect. Verified by review of each child's change against the
      inventory's rejection rationale.
